newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sligos, Axime in alliance talks.
newsitem.headline: Sligos, Axime in alliance talks.

text.p: French computer services and telecommunications company Sligos and computer systems firm Axime said on Monday that they were in advanced alliance talks.
"The managements of Sligos and Axime announce that they are in advanced talks aimed at establishing an industrial alliance between the two groups," the companies said in a joint statement.
Trade in shares of Sligos and Axime, 26.1 percent held by Paribas Affaires Industrielles, a unit of Paribas, were temporarily suspended at the companies' request.
The announcement said that the work councils of the two companies and their boards of directors had been summoned to a meeting to be held on Tuesday.
It added that further information would be released as soon as possible.
A spokeswoman for Axime said the deal "involved a potential business combination" and said she could make no further comment. Sligos also would not comment further.
A news conference is to be held on Wednesday in Paris at 1300 GMT.
Sligos, one of France's biggest computer services group, last month announced it planned to resume a programme of acquisitions broken off in 1994.
Press reports said it was looking at buying computer services companies operating in France and Germany.
The company, which returned to profit in 1995, is reported to have a war chest of 1.5 billion francs and no borrowings.
Sligos is 56.8 percent owned by the state-backed rescue vehicle Consortum de Realisation (CDR) set up to sell off assets owned by struggling French bank Credit Lyonnais.
The CDR said last January it had decided not to sell its stake in Sligos for at least two years to give the company time to complete its restructuring.
